title: Why Most Startups Miss Out on R&D Tax Credits
summary: Why Most Startups Miss Out on R&D Tax Credits
body_markdown:
Building a startup means making a lot of bets.


You hire engineers before you have a perfect product. You invest in experiments that may not work. You spend time solving problems that have never been solved before.


That’s exactly the kind of work the R&D tax credit was created to support.


But many startups never claim it.


Some founders assume they aren’t eligible because they aren’t a traditional research company. Others think the process is too complicated or only applies to large corporations. And some simply don’t realize they qualify until it’s too late.


The result? Startups leave valuable tax savings on the table.


## What counts as R&D for startups?


A common misconception is that research and development only applies to scientific labs or companies creating new technology from scratch.


In reality, many startups are doing qualifying R&D every day.


Your company may qualify if your team is working to develop or improve things like:


- Software products and platforms
- New features or functionality
- Technical infrastructure
- Automation systems
- Manufacturing processes
- Product prototypes
- New technology solutions


If your team is experimenting, testing, troubleshooting, and solving technical challenges, there’s a good chance some of that work could qualify.


## Why startups miss out on the R&D tax credit


**1. They assume they are too early**


Many founders think tax credits are something to worry about later, once they have revenue or a larger team.


But[early-stage startups](https://fondo.com/blog/where-are-you-really-a-breakdown-of-early-startup-stages) are often the ones doing the most experimentation. If you’re investing in product development, engineering, or technical problem-solving, you may already have qualifying activities.


**2. They don’t track qualifying expenses**


The R&D tax credit is tied to specific activities and expenses, not just whether your company has an R&D department.


Eligible expenses can include things like:


- Employee wages for qualifying work
- Certain contractor costs
- Supplies used during development


Without proper tracking, it’s easy for qualifying expenses to get overlooked.


**3. They think the process is too complicated**


The credit does require documentation, but that doesn’t mean founders need to spend weeks digging through old projects and spreadsheets.


The key is having a clear process for identifying qualifying activities and expenses.


For many startups, the biggest challenge isn’t eligibility. It’s knowing[where to start](https://fondo.com/blog/why-starrt-up-taxes-feel-so-stressful) .


## Why the R&D tax credit matters for startups


For startups, every dollar of runway matters.


The R&D tax credit can help offset some of the costs of building your product and give your company additional cash to invest in growth.


For eligible startups, the credit can even be applied against payroll taxes in certain situations, helping companies preserve cash before they are profitable.


That extra runway can mean more time to hire, improve your product, and reach your next milestone.


## Don’t leave money behind


Your startup is already investing in innovation. The R&D tax credit exists to reward companies doing exactly that.


The biggest mistake founders make is[waiting until tax season](https://fondo.com/blog/the-hidden-cost-of-cleaning-it-up-later) to think about it.


Start tracking qualifying activities early, understand what may qualify, and make sure you’re taking advantage of every opportunity available to your company.
